classification.difficultyReason: Applies the triangle angle sum, sometimes after identifying opposite or alternate angles.

content.prompt: Use the interior angle sum of a triangle to find $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ or $\theta$ in the diagrams below.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with the three interior angle labels.
spec.mathematics: Angles B=70 degrees, C=30 degrees; find angle A.

spec.description: Thin triangle IBT; one 20-degree annotation has two leaders, targeting the interior sectors at I and T.
spec.mathematics: Angles I and T are each 20 degrees; beta is angle IBT.

answer.worked:
Both leader arrows give $20^\circ$. Angle sum of $\triangle IBT$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+20^\circ+20^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-40^\circ\\\beta&=140^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Triangle CUT with a coordinate-derived right-angle square at T.
spec.mathematics: Angle T=90 degrees and U=35 degrees.
Angles A=85 degrees and B=81 degrees.

spec.description: Triangle QOP with QON and POM straight; alpha is above O.
spec.mathematics: Angles Q=35 degrees, P=72 degrees; alpha is vertically opposite QOP.

answer.worked:
Angle sum of $\triangle QOP$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle QOP+35^\circ+72^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle QOP&=73^\circ\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\alpha=73^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $O$).

spec.description: Triangle BRK with BKE and RKT straight.
spec.mathematics: Angle R=37 degrees; exterior crossing angle TKE=100 degrees.

answer.worked:
$\angle BKR=100^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $K$). Angle sum of $\triangle BRK$:
$$\begin{align*}\beta+37^\circ+100^\circ&=180^\circ\\\beta&=43^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three intersecting lines form triangle UTI. Both endpoints of the ascending line retain the printed label L.
spec.mathematics: Opposite angles give interior angles U=60 degrees and I=60 degrees; gamma is opposite the interior angle at T.

answer.worked:
$\angle TUI=60^\circ$ and $\angle UIT=60^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
Angle sum of $\triangle UTI$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle UTI+60^\circ+60^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle UTI&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\gamma=60^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $T$).

spec.description: Lines FABG, LACM and SCBR; no right-angle square at A.
spec.mathematics: Angle RBG=41 degrees and SCM=49 degrees; theta=FAL.
spec.answerVisibility: Theta remains unknown; no inferred perpendicular mark.

answer.worked:
$\angle ABC=41^\circ$ and $\angle ACB=49^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles).
Angle sum of $\triangle ABC$:
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC+41^\circ+49^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle BAC&=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
Thus $\theta=90^\circ$ (vertically opposite angles at $A$).

spec.description: Parallel lines PCAQ and RBS, matching arrow marks, triangle CAB. At B the sectors are alpha, gamma, 70 degrees from left to right.
spec.mathematics: ACB=60 degrees, ABS=70 degrees; alpha=RBC, beta=CAB, gamma=CBA.

answer.short:
$\alpha=60^\circ$, $\beta=70^\circ$, $\gamma=50^\circ$.

Use alternate angles, then the triangle angle sum.
answer.worked:
$\alpha=60^\circ$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel RS$).

$\beta=70^\circ$ (alternate angles, $PQ\parallel RS$).

Angle sum of $\triangle CAB$:
$$\begin{align*}\gamma+60^\circ+70^\circ&=180^\circ\\\gamma&=50^\circ\end{align*}$$
